title: No System 2 planner: every multi-step demo flow ends 'coming soon'
detail: MULTI_STEP (and ANSWER) routes say a canned line and return. prompts/planner_system.md is not loaded by any code (git grep planner_system in ml/ app/ bench/ = 0 hits), there is no planner model runtime, no observe->plan->act loop, no diff feedback. Browser task, Numbers finance and Premiere editing are all MULTI_STEP by the router's own taxonomy (SPEC G2: 30% finance, 15% Premiere, 20% browser), so 3 of the 4 demo flows and every 5-step task cannot run; HobbyLM/DeskMind task benchmarks score 0 on anything multi-step.
evidence: orchestrator.py@b438799:149 `if label == "MULTI_STEP": await self.server.say("Multi-step tasks are coming soon")`; evals/route_v1.jsonl has 16/128 MULTI_STEP cases (largest label).
fix: Add brain/planner.py now (before more router polish): load planner_system.md with {catalog} filled once (static prefix -> cached KV, like decision.py), user msg = goal + observe text (or act diff_text) + last <=5 actions/results; mlx_lm stream_generate with stop on 5 lines/blank; parse each completed line with dsl.parse and hand it to execute_actions immediately (design rule 'execute first action while decoding'); loop until done/ask/refuse/confirm-no or 8 turns. Start with the already-downloaded Qwen3.5-4B/9B 4-bit; swap to 35B-A3B if the speed lab allows.

title: Runtime router prompt differs from training render (LoRA mismatch)
detail: Training (cloud/data-pipeline training/src/muselet_train/catalog.py) renders special options with catalog.json special_options descriptions and arg signatures with enum values and ' optional'. Runtime hardcodes different special descriptions and drops enum values/optional. The Phase-1 LoRA will be served a system prompt it never saw (whole static prefix after token 674 differs) and ARGS signatures it never saw; the SPEC 1.7 parity gate (>=97% top-1) will fail or, worse, silently lose accuracy. Also both branches commit training/artifacts/route_render_samples.jsonl with different schemas (wip: {kind:id_list}/{i,utterance,tokens,decoded}; cloud: {kind:header}/{kind:route,context,label_token,...}) -> merge conflict, and wip's copy is not the training reference.
evidence: reviews/architect/tests/test_render_drift.py on wip b438799: all 4 special descriptions mismatch; runtime sig 'query:string required, kind:enum' vs train 'query:string required, kind:enum any|pdf|image|video|document|folder optional'. Token LCP of sample 1 (wip) vs sample 1 (cloud): 674; wip line `choice#6 = "MULTI_STEP": needs several actions, apps or UI steps` vs cloud `...: The request needs several UI steps or apps; hand off to the planner.`
fix: decision.py: read special descriptions from catalog['special_options']; port _arg_sig verbatim from muselet_train/catalog.py (or import muselet_train.route_render directly in the runtime). Drop wip's route_render_samples.jsonl, take cloud's, and add an ml test that re-renders every `kind:route` sample and asserts tokens + choice_pos equal (skip if tokenizer not cached).

title: premiere_command and start_timer route fine, then throw notImplemented
detail: Both are in skills/catalog.json, in the router's choice list and in the eval set (6 premiere_command + 3 start_timer cases), but Skills.run has no case for them -> default `throw HandsError.notImplemented`. The Premiere demo's instant commands ('cut here', 'add a marker', 'export') and the planner prompt rule 9 ('prefer skill premiere_command') all dead-end. The UXP bridge on cloud/fixtures-docs dials ws://127.0.0.1:8766, but nothing in ml/ listens on 8766, and its razor/undo are not_supported anyway.
evidence: git grep premiere_command origin/wip/local -- app -> 0 hits; HandsKitTests.swift:364-368 asserts start_timer == notImplemented; git grep 8766 -- ml -> 0 hits.
fix: Implement premiere_command in Swift as keystrokes to the activated 'Adobe Premiere Pro' process: razor_at_playhead=cmd+k, add_marker=m, play_toggle=space, undo=cmd+z, go_to_start=home, go_to_end=end, export=cmd+m (then planner handles the dialog). ~30 lines, no plugin needed for the demo. start_timer: Clock app via `open clock://` or a brain-side asyncio timer + mascot bubble. Bridge (8766 server in brain) only after the planner exists.

title: Router context is always app=none; online check stale and blocking
detail: self._ctx is initialised once and never updated (no write to _ctx anywhere), so every route sees app=none focused=none selection=no last_action=none. Training spends 3,000 G3 context-pair items + follow-up items on exactly these fields ('cut this' in Premiere -> premiere_command; 'a bit more' after set_volume -> change_volume); at runtime they can never fire. online= comes from decision._online_ok: a blocking 0.5 s TCP connect to 8.8.8.8 inside route() on the asyncio loop, cached 30 s -> right after 'turn off Wi-Fi' the router still believes online=yes for up to 30 s, and on a bad venue network one instant command per 30 s pays +500 ms. Also `--tau` is parsed (cli.py:158) but never passed to Orchestrator.
evidence: grep '_ctx\[' orchestrator.py@b438799 -> none; decision.py:116-121,217-221; cli.py:56 `Orchestrator(server, Catalog.load(), Tracer(), engine=engine)` without tau.
fix: Have the app include `app` (frontmost localizedName) and `focused` summary in the utterance frame (AGENTS.md contract addition, ~0 ms; it already knows NSWorkspace.frontmostApplication) and set _ctx from it; set _ctx['last_action'] = 'set_volume level=30' after each successful skill; after a wifi skill set online explicitly; move the reachability probe to a background task (SCNetworkReachability-equivalent on the Swift side is better). Pass tau through.

title: Partials dropped; ARGS decode always serial after release
detail: The app sends partial utterances every 450 ms (VoiceController.swift:166-185) but the server ignores non-final frames, so route+args start only after release + 60 ms tail + full-clip Parakeet re-transcribe. Then orchestrator calls engine.args for every skill, including zero-arg skills (sleep_display, battery_status, todays_agenda, copy_selection) and bool/enum ones, as up-to-32-token greedy decode with a per-token full Python round trip. Instant-command budget today (estimates, unmeasured end-to-end): STT final ~? + route ~15-40 ms + args ~8-20 tokens x ~10-20 ms = 80-400 ms + skill ms; route/args run synchronously on the event loop. The route+args part can be ~0 on the critical path.
evidence: server.py@b438799:104 `if msg.get("final"):`; orchestrator.py:165 unconditional `self.engine.args(label, ...)`; decision.py:342 `for _ in range(32)` with np.argmax per step.
fix: On each partial: run route (+args if p_top>=tau) in a worker thread keyed by normalized text; on final, if normalize(final)==normalize(last speculated), execute the cached decision immediately. Skip args when the skill has no args; for single bool/enum args use one more choice question (one forward pass) instead of decode. Measure and trace release->skill_start ms as the headline number vs HobbyLM's 0.26 s.

title: Executor drops expects and ends batches at scripts; prompt promises otherwise
detail: (a) `if op == "script": return await self._script(a)` returns after the first script, silently skipping later actions and reporting ok. (b) _script builds params {op,lang,code} and _skill sends {name,args}: any `expect` the planner attached to a script/skill is discarded, so rule 3 and design rule 'every consequential action carries an expect' are unenforced on the two most-recommended paths (rule 1 + Numbers rule 8). (c) `done` is said verbatim with no verification, yet prompt example 3 emits `done` in the same batch as the write script, before any observation (contradicts prompt rule 4 and AGENTS 'DONE is verified by the harness'). (d) Prompt says click x,y are 0-1000 image coords; Act.swift:272-281 clicks them as global points and the brain does no conversion (and has no screenshot path at all) -> every pixel click lands in the top-left 1000x1000 pt. (e) Prompt lists `script applescript|jxa`; AGENTS.md/dsl.py also allow shell.
evidence: orchestrator.py@b438799:287,328; Act.swift@b438799:272-281 `let p = CGPoint(x: x, y: y)`; planner_system.md@cdae5d9:20,23,66-71.
fix: script: `r = await self._script(a); if r != 'ok': return r; continue`; pass a.get('expect') into the script act params and run `verify {expect}` after a skill when present; on `done` call verify on the last expect (or re-observe and hand it to the planner once) before saying success; convert click coords brain-side using the screenshot's {origin, width, height, scale}; fix example 3 to end with `expect`/no done and let the next turn emit done.

title: No benchmark harness exists for HobbyLM, DeskMind, JevBench or typed decisions
detail: bench/ contains only speed_lab.py (synthetic shapes) and run_when_ready.sh; there is no /v1/systemone shim, no HobbyLM 125-task runner, no DeskMind Bench (13 tasks) runner, no JevBench or typed-decisions adapter. 'Beat them on their own benchmarks' is the headline claim and needs >= a day of harness work. Fairness notes: HobbyLM's 0.26 s is median decision latency with a fixed action vocabulary and no vision, so compare our route p50 (warm cache, same utterances) not end-to-end; its 72% is live task success on 125 tasks -> we must run all 125 live on the Mac (not a subset) and report failures. DeskMind Bench is 13 live macOS tasks scored by success -> needs the planner (architect-1). SPEC 1.5 dedups against HobbyLM data/frozen tests (good), but evals/route_v1.jsonl is hand-written and should not be reported as a public number.
evidence: git ls-tree origin/main bench/ -> run_when_ready.sh, speed_lab.py; git grep -i 'systemone|hobbylm|deskmind bench|jevbench' -- ml bench evals -> only a model id in speed_lab.py docstring.
fix: Build in this order: (1) brain HTTP endpoint POST /v1/systemone {state, questions} -> distributions (wraps DecisionEngine.route) so HobbyLM's/typed-decisions scripts can call us unchanged (~2 h); (2) HobbyLM task adapter mapping their fixed vocab -> our skills, run all 125 live, log per-task (~3 h); (3) DeskMind Bench runner once planner exists. Publish latency with identical measurement points (first token/decision after text available).

title: Phase-1 LoRA likely misses Sat 12:00 PDT; no fallback router measured
detail: At 2026-10-24 05:14Z (Fri 22:14 PDT) the cloud branch is at SPEC step 3 (2% sample, waiting for approval). Still to go: full G1/G2/G3 generation via Anthropic/OpenAI Batch APIs (SLA up to 24 h), soft-label teacher pass, adjudication batch, dedup, 2-run LR pilot, approval, full run, merge, MLX convert, parity. That is 3 serial batch round-trips + 2 approvals in ~14 h. If it slips, the demo runs the zero-shot base 4B (cli.py default) with a prompt the eval has not measured, and the 'beat HobbyLM' latency/accuracy claim has no model behind it.
evidence: git log origin/cloud/data-pipeline: 5da307e 'G1/G2/G3 generation + 2% sample report' (04:55Z); SPEC.md:22 deadline; cli.py:20-21 default candidates Qwen3.5-4B-4bit/0.8B-4bit base.
fix: Lead decision: approve the 2% sample now and cap full generation at ~15K items using non-batch (synchronous, parallel) API calls for the first slice so training can start by ~08:00 PDT; skip adjudication except for labels with high disagreement. Meanwhile run `brain eval-route` on route_v1.jsonl with base 0.8B and 4B today (after fixing architect-2) to have a measured fallback and pick tau.

evidence: decision.py@bcd3b75 now takes special descriptions from catalog.special_options (catalog_options) and ports _arg_sig verbatim; route_render_samples.jsonl now byte-identical to cloud/data-pipeline 56ef91b. Not run: decision.py has a SyntaxError at line 389 in this snapshot (looks mid-edit). Still recommended: an ml test that re-renders every kind:route sample.

Still open @bcd3b75: script return ends the batch (orchestrator.py:287), expect dropped for script/skill (328, _skill), done unverified, click 0-1000 coords vs global points (prompt:20, Act.swift:272-281), no screenshot path.
